top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks. The magic-wavelength condition cancels the light shift so many atoms can be interrogated at once, which is what makes 1e-18 accuracy and stability practical. This is a separable invention from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, it has been reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, and two names map onto the concept and the record realisation. The citation must stay narrow and name the lattice scheme, not frequency metrology in general. Unverified early-priority questions (Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto) are a reservation, not grounds to withhold, so no award ranks last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; University of Tokyo and JSPS fellowships and exchanges with Japanese universities are noted for Katori, but no documented personal or collaborative tie to Katori or Ye
